name: Eleadah
overview: Eleadah was a male member of the tribe of Ephraim, identified uniquely as the son of Tahath. His life is briefly noted in Scripture with the significant detail that he was killed by the men of Gath, marking a violent end to his story. This highlights the ongoing conflicts faced by the tribes of Israel in their history.
namesAndTitles: The name Eleadah means 'G-d has adorned,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that acknowledges God's blessing or favor. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a clear reference to divine adornment or honor.
familyAndRelationships: Eleadah is explicitly recorded as the son of Tahath, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further family connections, so his lineage is limited to this father-son link.
scriptureSignificance: Eleadah's significance lies in his identification as a descendant of Ephraim and as a victim of hostile action by the men of Gath. His death illustrates the dangers and hostilities encountered by the tribes of Israel during their settlement and struggles. Though his mention is brief, it contributes to the broader narrative of tribal histories and conflicts in the Old Testament.
